text: The NSA in 1992 guessed plaintext autokey on K1 and K2's system. Autokey had only been tried with the sculpture's alphabets and word alphabets; here the alphabet may be in any order.
Each known letter past the primer gives an equation in the alphabet's places alone; a search over the 26 places decides every lag exactly, for K4 and ten scrambled copies.
K4 fits as many lags as the copies in every kind and form, and has 4 rare fits against up to 27 for a copy. Dead lags closed; fitting ones would need the English decider, about an hour each.
